### Round log (pilot run, SF1 data, old geomean bar)
- E0001/E0002 contains-selectivity 0.04: retired at SF1 (the plan did not change). At SF10 the plan flips, and it was accepted as E0008.
- E0003 estimate-gated perfect hash agg: q13 -24% but q17 +64%. Estimate gating is the wrong mechanism.
- E0004/E0007 lazy-init perfect HT plus an 18-bit extension: retired (q02 +8%). q13's c_custkey range at SF10 is 1.5M (21 bits), out of reach anyway.
- E0006 run-collapse in agg probe: about 10% less agg CPU, no wall gain. The cost is group creation/finalize, not probing.

### New run (SF10 data; bar: some templates faster beyond noise, none slower)
- G1R1: E0008 contains-selectivity ACCEPTED (q09 1211 -> 709ms).
- G1R2: E0009 per-key BF for multi-key joins ACCEPTED (q09 -15 to -19%).
- G2R1: E0010 OR-filter derivation under a root AND ACCEPTED (q19 347 -> 186, q14 faster). Follow-up: derive from deeper-nested ORs (q07 gained nothing; unclear why).
- G2R2: E0011 Deliminator SEMI/ANTI without blocking ops ACCEPTED (q04 -30%, q22 -20%, q02). Geomean 236.9ms (1.133x).
- G3R1: dispatched "Join filters for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI + equality for deliminated EXISTS". Evidence: join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:207-219 returns early for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI, which is safe to allow because the output comes from the build side. :237 skips NOT_DISTINCT_FROM. After E0011, q04 is a RIGHT_SEMI with a 37.9M lineitem probe, 574k orders build, 0.89s join, and no filter on lineitem. A manual SEMI JOIN with = was still unfiltered (182-210 vs 214ms), so part A (allowing RIGHT_SEMI) is the main lever. If it fails on perf: check whether the BF was runtime-disabled, or whether CM projections block the pushdown target (in the manual test, CM off still showed no filter, but RIGHT_SEMI was excluded then). If part B causes correctness trouble, drop it and land part A alone (it helps IN subqueries with = conditions).

### Lessons for dispatching
- Keep diffs out of widely included headers. Use file-local statics.
- Ask implementers to EXPLAIN-check before the full bench. Bench noise is +-10-35% per template on single runs; re-run before calling a regression.
- `dbe-tool sql "q; q; q"` prints per-statement ms; the first run is cold (2-3x slower). Pipe a single dbe-tool call into `| cut -c1-90 | tail -N`; that works without approval. EXPLAIN ANALYZE output is truncated at about 110 lines.
- MANUAL REWRITE TEST = cheap validation of optimizer ideas (it worked for E0010 and E0011). `SET disabled_optimizers='x'; q` works in one sql call.
- rules.md: never change default settings.
- Planner estimates after LIKE filters and outer joins are off by 5-1000x.
- VERIFY probe/build sides in the plan before proposing join ideas; plans change after every accepted plan change.

### Codebase facts (verified)
- HASH_JOIN: LEFT child = probe, RIGHT child = build. BFs only reach probe-side scans.
- Join filter generation: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:206). The join-type exclusion list is at 207. compute_aggregates_anyway (perfect HT) applies to INNER/1 cond/EQUAL only. Physical side: physical_hash_join.cpp Sink 339, Finalize 1006-1025.
- Join BF: CanUseBloomFilter in physical_hash_join.cpp (multi-key since E0009); a perfect HT disables the BF.
- Perfect hash JOIN (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:66 CanDoPerfectHashJoin): INNER only, 1 condition, range <= 1,048,576.
- Compressed materialization (compress_comparison_join.cpp) wraps join keys in __internal_compress_* projections. Disabling it gave no wall gain on q18/q09. Deprioritized.
- Expression rewriter rule order: optimizer.cpp:50-71. JoinDependentFilter handles a root OR and a root AND (E0010).
- Deliminator (deliminator.cpp): Optimize at 69 (the E0011 SEMI/ANTI skip is at 88). RemoveJoinWithDelimGet at 205 adds IS NOT NULL for plain =/<> conditions (245-253). The delim join keeps NOT DISTINCT FROM conditions after full removal.
- LIKE: like.cpp + contains.cpp (memchr-specialized). The q13 NOT LIKE scan cost is likely FSST decompression.
- Scan filter estimate: relation_statistics_helper.cpp ExtractGetStats.
- Perfect hash agg: plan_aggregate.cpp:127. Radix adaptation: radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424.

### SF10 profile (G3 start, wall ms): q13 684, q18 670, q09 670, q05 258, q03 245, q08 223, q17 216, q04 207, q19 191, q07 190, q16 166, q22 147, q14 129, q02 79.
- q13: orders scan NOT LIKE 2.72s CPU; RIGHT join (15M probe, 1.5M build) 1.78s; HASH_GROUP_BY 2.50s.
- q09: lineitem scan (BF-cut to 3.27M); o_orderkey join 1.79s (orders 15M, no dynamic filter).
- q18: subquery agg over 60M lineitem -> 15M groups dominates.

### Directions
- Active: RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI join filters (q04, q22?, q18 IN?, hidden EXISTS/IN).
- Next candidates: (a) left ANTI join filters are impossible, but RIGHT_ANTI is covered above. (b) q09 o_orderkey join: orders 15M on the unfiltered side, so look at a build flip or filter. (c) Perfect hash join for RIGHT/SEMI joins (q13 needs a range above 1M). (d) q13/q18 high-cardinality agg (backlog; profile first). (e) Deeper-nested OR derivation (q07?). Manual-test first.
- Low value: CM blocking pushdown.
- Exhausted: estimate-gated perfect hash agg; agg duplicate-run collapse; LIKE matcher micro-opts.

issues.title: Join filters (min-max + bloom) for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI probes and equality for deliminated EXISTS conditions
issues.hypothesis: After E0011, q04 runs as one HASH_JOIN RIGHT_SEMI: probe = lineitem (37.9M rows after l_commitdate<l_receiptdate, from a 60M scan), build = filtered orders (574k rows). The join takes 0.89s CPU and the lineitem scan gets NO dynamic or bloom filter. There are two blockers, both verified in code. (1) JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters (src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:207-219) returns early for RIGHT_SEMI and RIGHT_ANTI. That is overly conservative: in both types the output comes from the build side, so a probe row whose key is not in the build can never affect the result. Only left ANTI, MARK, SINGLE, LEFT and OUTER really need every probe row. (2) The deliminated delim join keeps its condition as `o_orderkey IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o_orderkey`, and GenerateJoinFilters skips COMPARE_NOT_DISTINCT_FROM (line 237). In Deliminator::RemoveJoinWithDelimGet (deliminator.cpp:245-253), each removed plain =/<> correlation condition already adds an IS NOT NULL filter on the subquery-side column. With the RHS key known non-NULL, NOT DISTINCT FROM is equivalent to = for SEMI, ANTI and INNER (a NULL LHS key matches nothing either way). Manual test: rewriting q04 as an explicit SEMI JOIN with = gives the same RIGHT_SEMI plan, still unfiltered because of blocker (1), and 182-210ms vs 214ms. So blocker (2) alone gains little, and the main gain needs (1). The build covers about 3 months of 7 years of orders, so a bloom filter on l_orderkey should cut the probe rows about 15-25x.
issues.plan: A. src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp GenerateJoinFilters: remove RIGHT_SEMI and RIGHT_ANTI from the early-return list. Keep MARK, SINGLE, LEFT, OUTER and ANTI, and update the comment to say why the right-variants are safe. Leave compute_aggregates_anyway INNER-only, so the perfect-HT behaviour does not change. Check physical_hash_join.cpp (Sink line 339, Finalize 1006-1025) and the bloom filter code (CanUseBloomFilter/PushBloomFilter) for join-type assumptions. B. src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp Deliminator::Optimize: when the candidate is fully removed (the type is changed to LOGICAL_COMPARISON_JOIN at line 109) and every removed correlation condition was a plain COMPARE_EQUAL (so an IS NOT NULL filter was added for each delim column), rewrite the delim_join conditions from COMPARE_NOT_DISTINCT_FROM to COMPARE_EQUAL. Do this only for join_type SEMI, ANTI or INNER, and track it with a local flag. Do not do it if any removed condition was NOT DISTINCT FROM or DISTINCT FROM. Use file-local statics only, with no header changes. Validate with EXPLAIN ANALYZE of q04.m0: the lineitem scan should show a dynamic/bloom filter on l_orderkey and far fewer than 37.9M rows into the join. Also check q22 and q18, where the IN subquery may be RIGHT_SEMI. Correctness: NOT EXISTS and EXISTS with NULL keys on both sides, a RIGHT_ANTI case where the build has keys absent from the probe, and an IN subquery, all checked against unoptimized results (SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown').
issues.expected_gain: q04 207ms -> roughly 120-150ms (the join is 0.89s CPU, and most of the lineitem scan/filter feeding it is avoidable). q22 and q18 possibly, if their semi/anti joins are right-flipped. Geomean about 2-4%. Hidden EXISTS, NOT EXISTS and IN templates (TPC-H q20/q21-like) likely benefit.
issues.generality: Any EXISTS, IN or NOT EXISTS subquery, or explicit semi/anti join, where the optimizer puts the small outer side on the build (RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI) and the big table on the probe. That is a very common analytical pattern. Possible slowdowns: unselective filters add bloom/min-max probing cost on scans, but the existing selectivity-based runtime disable mitigates that, the same as for INNER joins.
issues.risk: Medium-low. Correctness risk is in part B's NULL semantics (limited to fully-deliminated joins whose correlation conditions were all plain equality with IS NOT NULL added) and in any hidden join-type assumption in the physical filter code. The diff is small and in two .cpp files.
